>Annoying and not very professional compared to whom, and to what?

>available to do this kind of thing, with the "other" card game out there,

There are a lot of CCGs out there. There are a handful of companies. AFAIK,
most provide checklists of some sort.

>> or should we simply cease all trading for the first month?
>
>You are getting slighty hysterical about this issue. Please take a deep
>breath and try and relax.

Yes, don't trade. I don't think there's a need to until critical information
is available.

OTOH, I don't understand the lack of information. It does not slow down the
release of a product to add a checklist. It does not slow down the release of
a product to post an official spoiler/checklist up on the web site. It does
not help anyone to not have that info available.

Actually, on a bit of a tangent, I delayed posting about the prerelease as I
believed that that was what was desired in order for the cards to be a surprise
to those who hadn't yet played. But, there was no reprimand for all of those
who spoiled cards prior to Sunday's event(s), so I guess no one cares.

So, I don't understand what the position of WW is.

Messages.Author: Rob Grau
Messages.Body:
I think Ben makes a most valid point here.

If I recall from Sabbat War, the WW folks provided a card list to the CCG
magazines after the release, but waited about a month or so to release it to
the public b/c the CCG magazines were more likely to publish a list if there
wasn't already an official one in cyberspace.

This doesn't bother me as long as it doesn't impact tournament play.
